newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SAYS OUTLOOK FOR SEMICONDUCTORS BRIGHT.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SAYS OUTLOOK FOR SEMICONDUCTORS BRIGHT.

text.p: Philips Electronics NV said on Thursday growth prospects for its semiconductor business looked healthy, with strong demand from customers and signs that price erosion was coming to an end.
"We have seen that the price erosion for semiconductors really has slowed down and in fact almost came to a stop in the second quarter," CFO Jan Hommen told a news conference.

Hommen said the relationship between supply and demand in the semiconductor industry was developing favourably and that new orders were coming in at a faster rate than products were being shipped to customers.

"We are operating our facilities at a very high rate of capacity. Demand is excellent for the products that we are associated with, especially the consumer products and also the multimedia chips are doing extremely well," he said.

"Our book-to-bill (ratio) is very much in excess of one...and has been building up over time. So that is another sign that we are getting more bookings in than we are basically producing and shipping," he said.
Hommen said some industry analysts were forecasting growth in demand for semiconductors of about 15 percent per year.
Philips would debottleneck production capacity in order to squeeze more output from its existing plants, he said.
Operating profits from Philips' components and semiconductors division rose to 1.06 billion guilders in the first half of 1997 from 908 million in the first half of 1996.
